title: SciTeX StatusCode, spec_version 1
description: Three fields. `kind` is a discriminated-union tag saying HOW TO READ `code`; `code` is the NATIVE code within that kind, preserved verbatim with no translation; `message` is a HINT that declares what the sender is doing and hands the receiver the means to verify and to ask. NOTE: this schema is a FLOOR. Three rules cannot be expressed in JSON Schema and are enforced by the validator instead: (1) `code` must be in the declared kind's enumerated domain, sourced from kinds.yaml; (2) `message` must contain no inferred-cause marker (rule M1); (3) for codes marked requires_probe (http 102, http 202) `message` must name a runnable probe (rule M2). A document that passes this schema may still be refused at construction. See status-codes.md sec.7.

kind.description: Which status system `code` is borrowed from. NOT a SciTeX vocabulary — a tag saying which dictionary to open. Each call boundary declares the kind it borrows; see boundaries.yaml.

code.description: The native code, verbatim. `http`/`process` carry an integer; `grpc`/`dns`/`errno`/`scitex` carry a string. errno carries the NAME, never the number, because errno numbers are platform-specific and would change meaning in transit.

message.description: A hint, not an assertion. Answers: what to DO, what the sender IS doing, and HOW TO ASK. Verification belongs to the receiver and this field hands over the instrument.

ok.description: FORBIDDEN. Derive it (`kind == 'http' and 200 <= code < 300`, `kind == 'process' and code == 0`, ...). Two fields that can disagree will eventually disagree, and a reader then has to guess which one to trust.

retryable.description: FORBIDDEN. Readable from the code within the declared kind (503 yes, 403 no), and `message` carries the useful version ('retry in 10s, or poll `...`'), which is strictly more actionable than a boolean.
